en.question: A team wants to bypass optional review for low-consequence drafts whenever the assistant writes 'confidence: 0.97'. No relationship between that number and correctness has been measured. High-consequence actions already have mandatory review. What should happen before using confidence to route the optional-review cases?

options.text: Interpret 0.97 as a 97% probability of correctness because the value is expressed on a zero-to-one scale.
options.note: The numeric format does not establish calibration. A generated probability-like value can accompany confidently incorrect content.

options.text: Ask the assistant to explain its score and bypass review whenever the explanation contains a source citation.
options.note: The score explanation and citation can themselves be unsupported. Neither demonstrates an empirical relationship between the signal and task correctness.

options.text: Evaluate the routing signal on representative adjudicated tasks, including error severity and scope limits, while retaining mandatory-review rules.
options.note: Representative labeled outcomes can establish whether the signal supports a useful routing decision for the stated task. Calibration evidence does not create an exception to separate mandatory controls.

options.text: Reuse a published confidence threshold from another application and monitor user complaints after automatic release begins.
options.note: Calibration and error consequences depend on the task and deployment distribution. Another application's cutoff and delayed complaints do not validate this signal before use.
